limitations.sourceForm: setNMIExclusive in the selected C64 profile
limitations.reason: The approved private-home-free exclusive route has proved idle-entry CIA2 source ownership, immutable links, direct output and four-profile timer/RESTORE/boundary VICE behavior with vector-first final handback. External aggregate stack, retained-firmware completion, physical behavior and general startup preservation remain unproved; this bounded qualification does not grant raw takeover or arbitrary prior-source ownership.
limitations.decision: RD-05 CIA2 ownership plan AR-P2/AR-P3; independent source/storage/output qualification and 568 native cases without skips. RD-05/DEF-7, keyboard coexistence and mandatory R5.4 startup-state repair remain open. VICE-verified / hardware-unverified.

limitations.sourceForm: balanced setNMI/restoreNMI in the selected C64 profile
limitations.reason: The approved private-home-free generated stock-chained route passes storage, immutable-link, actual output and four-profile genuine-source VICE qualification. Per-entry storage and stack facts are proved; external aggregate stack, unrestricted nesting and complete retained-firmware completion remain unproved and are not promised.
limitations.decision: RD-05 cooperative NMI plan AR-P11; independent source, storage, output and genuine-source VICE qualification; exclusive takeover and remaining DEF-7 obligations stay RD-05-owned

limitations.sourceForm: setIRQ, setIRQExclusive, or restoreIRQ reached during IRQ-handler execution
limitations.reason: Balanced handler-side IRQ updates have finite root-specific ownership, private storage and saved links; source, output and VICE qualification pass. An unmatched restore still fails with E10278.
limitations.decision: RD-05 handler-IRQ plan AR-P3; independent source, storage, output and VICE qualification

limitations.sourceForm: a deep mainline call path that cannot overlap an installed IRQ handler
limitations.reason: Static stack proof now follows actual installation, mask and call intervals; independent overlap and instruction-boundary regressions pass without changing emitted code
limitations.decision: Phase 6 RV-010 fixed and independently re-reviewed in Phase 9; stack-overlap, stack-overlap-contexts, stack-nonreturn, stack-mask-boundary and stack-mask-return specification tests

limitations.sourceForm: loadable const initialized by a native asset handler
limitations.reason: Native asset handlers now deliver loadable unit bytes through the RD-07 packager. The retired restriction was the resident-only handler boundary; the replacement probe builds a loadable native asset successfully.
limitations.decision: RD-07 delivered native loadable units; the ledger probe uses the synthetic SPD fixture and must build

limitations.sourceForm: setSpritePointer with more than one distinct vicScreenSelect screen
limitations.reason: The frozen setSpritePointer API has no screen argument. A unique compile-time screen base is required for a layout-derived pointer table; a program that selects two distinct screens cannot be resolved without a per-call screen relation. The rejection fails closed rather than writing the wrong table.
limitations.owner: T-27 follow-up / issue #140; future per-call screen relation
limitations.decision: RD-06 residual plan; single active screen is supported, multi-screen pointer-table selection remains tracked debt

limitations.sourceForm: an interrupt function that materializes a Boolean from a 16-bit word mask whose high byte can be nonzero, a computed/non-addressable runtime mask, or a comparison against a nonzero constant, or that retains more than eight bytes or keeps a retained local across a control-flow join or call
limitations.reason: The cooperative NMI route still admits no invocation-private RAM or zero-page homes. A word mask now joins both masked bytes with an inline branch, a computed mask is retained on the handler's own hardware stack and consumed as an absolute,X ALU operand, and a nonzero comparison materializes from A with CMP or the single-bit identity branch. The retention proof now spans control-flow joins and stack-balanced calls, uses a dominance slot plan, and is bounded by the platform hardware-stack capacity instead of a fixed eight bytes. All five probes build with no private home and the reported peak is exact.
limitations.decision: Issue #150 delivered the wide word-mask join, the computed runtime mask, the nonzero masked comparison, capacity-bounded retention, and multi-block/calling retention. The ledger probes are retained as the regression witnesses for the delivered forms; no residual source form remains in this row.

limitations.sourceForm: a retained local in an interrupt function installed through the stock chained setNMI route
limitations.reason: Hardware-stack retention is proved on the generated NMI entry shell, and both cooperative installers emit one. The chained route was never blocked by its frame: its entry shell balances, its indexed slot reads address it correctly, and its handover leaves the previous handler the frame it expects. What blocked it was a compiler limitation one level away - a frame unwind beyond six retained bytes raises the stack pointer in one go, and the flag proof treated that as making the stack unknowable, losing the status snapshot this route must restore before handing over. With the unwind followed by its recorded released-byte count, the route retains like the exclusive one and charges one byte more, which is the difference between the two declared entry frames.
limitations.decision: AR-P32 reverses AR-P11's chained-retention line under explicit authorization. The nine-sample chained fixture is converted from rejection to admission, mirroring the exclusive route's assertion set with a measured hardware-stack figure; a retaining helper stays rejected on either route, because retention is a property of the generated entry shell and a helper has none, and that helper case carries the canonical reentrancy witness.

limitations.sourceForm: c64.vic.vicSpriteBlock(&sheets[i]) with an element index chosen at run time
limitations.reason: A VIC field is one value resolved before the artifact is written. An index that varies at run time names a different element on every execution, so there is no single value to resolve, and the refusal fails closed rather than computing a block the chip will not fetch. The accepted spelling adds the run-time choice to the block number instead of to the address: the capability resolves one element address, the compiler follows the addition, and every selectable block stays inside the readable area.
limitations.owner: C64 video-field capability on module storage; future per-element block relation
limitations.decision: Deferred with a working spelling available and named by the refusal itself. The block-number form is accepted today and keeps every selectable block reachable, so no program is blocked by this restriction.

limitations.sourceForm: c64.vic.vicScreenSelect(&screen) or c64.vic.vicBitmapSelect(&bitmap) on ordinary module storage
limitations.reason: The pointer-tail reservation, the minimum fetched extent and the single-active-screen proof are carried only for an embedded asset. Accepting ordinary module storage would leave the eight sprite-pointer bytes at the end of a screen matrix owned by nobody, so an unrelated object could occupy them and move sprites, and would leave thousands of fetched bitmap bytes reserved by nobody regardless of how short the declaration is. Neither loss would be reported at run time. The sibling character-memory field is unaffected and accepts ordinary module storage, because it needs only alignment and a reachable run and a partial charset is legal.
limitations.owner: C64 screen and bitmap field storage; future module-storage reservation and active-screen proof
limitations.decision: Deferred; an embedded asset or a constant address works today, and the refusal names both spellings.

limitations.sourceForm: let a: word = &buffer; c64.vic.vicSpriteBlock(a), or a helper parameter reached only as publish(&buffer)
limitations.reason: Naming an address before using it and factoring a publishing helper are both ordinary modern code, and in both cases the address is settled at link time. The compiler does not propagate it through the binding or the parameter, so the field cannot attribute the value to one object and fails closed rather than computing a block from an address it cannot name. The refusal is honest about that cause and shows the direct spelling; what remains undelivered is the propagation, not the diagnosis.
limitations.owner: C64 video-field address resolution; future propagation through a single-assignment binding and a single-address parameter
limitations.decision: Deferred; passing the address straight to the field works today. The fix is address propagation through a single-assignment binding and through a parameter reached with one address, which would retire both source forms together.

limitations.reason: The zero-page allocator chooses homes for fast access and does not yet honour a video alignment requirement, so the field would resolve against an address the author never wrote and cannot predict. Reachability is not the problem: zero page is inside the chip's bank and outside the character-ROM window, so the data is readable there. It is the alignment that is unavailable, which is why the refusal names the storage rather than the address.
limitations.owner: C64 zero-page allocation and video alignment; future alignment-aware zero-page homes
limitations.decision: Deferred; declaring the data at module level works today and the refusal names that declaration site. Retiring this row needs the zero-page allocator to accept and honour an alignment requirement, not a change to the field.

limitations.sourceForm: let fs: fn(): byte[2] = [&one, &one]; with fs[0]()
limitations.reason: A table of function pointers dispatched by index is ordinary code in comparable systems languages and is the natural spelling of the jump table a 6502 programmer writes by hand constantly. A single function pointer works: 'let f: fn(): byte = &one;' followed by 'f()' builds and runs. Putting two of them in an array and calling through an element refuses the whole program, and refuses it with an internal code that names neither the unsupported construct nor a spelling that works. Nothing about the restriction is forced by the hardware.
limitations.owner: Function-pointer tables and indexed indirect calls; lowering an array of code addresses
limitations.decision: Deferred. Two things have to change and the row covers both: the construct has to be supported, and until it is the refusal has to name the array of function pointers at its declaration span instead of reporting an internal code. Retiring this row needs the indexed call to build; changing the diagnostic alone updates the recorded code and keeps the row open.
